what: From Andrew: turn blaze::hot_alloc on for blaze's own code. New AGENTS.md rule bump-allocate (tools/agents/rules.ts:70): task-lifetime collections name their allocator (Vec::new_in(frame) from blaze_mem::frame::current); a global allocation needs '// alloc: <why>'. Today blaze::hot is allowed by default and no manifest turns it on. Steps: (1) set it to warn in the root workspace manifest's [workspace.lints.blaze] (cargo ignores lint tools it does not know; blaze reads [lints.blaze]; the root edit is the coordinator's file, so put the exact lines in your report and I apply them) and count findings per crate. The coordinator runs one blaze check for the counts; until v2 checks itself, give the counts from tools/v2/hot_lint.py over the workspace and say how its rules differ from the lint's. (2) Deny it crate by crate, starting with hir-ty, hir-def, blaze-query and base-db, fixing each finding (new_in(frame)) or exempting it with '// alloc: <why>'. (3) A test, named for the property, that a fresh Vec::new() in a denied crate fails the check. Report the per-crate counts before any deny lands.
